output.methodChoice: Collected X10 (transmitted instructions and product-record history) and X11 (controller downloads and packing records). Compared outcomes across K1–K9 by carried temperature, carrier, fungicide stock, transit days and Lower Serra share.
output.brief:
The rejections trace to a setup error, not the fungicide, Lower Serra fruit or Meridane's equipment. When Meridane bookings moved to Tallis, the mandarin product record was created by copying the avocado record, and its 7.0°C carriage temperature was never changed to your 4.0°C specification. All five rejected containers ran at 7.0°C; the carrier's units held that setting within 0.4°C and your own loggers agree. Every container at 4.0°C passed whatever its carrier, fungicide or Lower Serra share, while one packed with the old fungicide failed at 7.0°C. I'm about 90% sure. Lower Serra pallets did decay more inside rejected containers, but other pallets were also far over tolerance; why is unproven because stowage wasn't recorded.

Next: correct the record to 4.0°C now; have Meridane reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct; check every booking's temperature against the specification before submission, and review other product records before Coastway joins Tallis. Don't claim against Meridane, or suspend and withhold pay from Lower Serra; reverting the fungicide isn't needed. Hold any Brindle deduction until the contract and your own sign-off are reviewed. Consider telling Nordhafen what you found and fixed.
